skill.name: large-report-editor
skill.description: Helps edit very large Markdown research reports with chunked edits, backup guidance, and strict citation requirements.
skill.summary: Edit large Markdown reports with structured, citation-aware changes.
skill.author: ACSKamloops

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code spans in SKILL.md. I found no executable shell command, prompt injection text, or semantic abuse intent in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: - Use backups in `99_Working_Files/Archive/` before major edits.

finding_verdicts.reason: The snippet is a Markdown bullet using backticks to format a referenced file path. It does not invoke Ruby, a shell, or user-controlled command execution.
The backticks mark an inline Markdown file path inside documentation text. There is no executable command, shell interpolation, or command injection surface.
The line uses Markdown inline code formatting for a backup directory path. It is not Ruby backtick execution and does not run external commands.

content.value_statement: Large Markdown reports are hard to revise without losing structure, sources, or context. This skill guides chunked edits, backups, and citation-aware changes for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides edits for very large Markdown research reports.
Requires cited new statements with StableID and page anchors.
Directs users to create backups before major edits.
Supports compiling report changes while preserving structure.
limitations: Does not include the referenced external instruction files in this package.
Does not perform fact checking without source material supplied by the user.
Does not provide automated citation validation or document parsing code.
Focused on Markdown reports, not spreadsheets or presentation files.

use_cases.title: Revise Legal Research Reports
use_cases.description: Revise long evidence-backed Markdown reports while preserving source references and page anchors.

use_cases.title: Compile Policy Briefing Files
use_cases.description: Compile sections from multiple research notes into a structured report with traceable citations.

use_cases.title: Update Technical Documentation
use_cases.description: Apply controlled edits to large Markdown documents without rewriting unaffected sections.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Report Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the large-report-editor skill to revise this Markdown section. Preserve structure and cite any new claims with StableID and page anchors.

prompt_templates.title: Citation Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this report chapter for uncited statements. List each issue and suggest citation-aware edits without adding unsupported facts.

prompt_templates.title: Chunked Compilation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a chunked editing plan for this large Markdown report. Include backup steps, section order, and citation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Multi-Source Rewrite
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this long report with the supplied source excerpts. Use surgical patches, preserve unaffected text, and cite every new statement precisely.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a safe edit of one long report section.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns a focused edit plan, identifies affected headings, and notes where citations are required before changing factual claims.

output_examples.input: A user provides source excerpts for a report update.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes chunked edits, names source anchors for new statements, and avoids changes outside the requested sections.

output_examples.input: A user asks to compile several Markdown drafts.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines merge order, backup checkpoints, and citation checks before producing the combined report text.

best_practices: Provide source excerpts with StableID and page anchors for any factual additions.
Ask for edits by section, heading, or chunk when the report is very large.
Create backups before major rewrites or compilation passes.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent facts or citations.
Do not edit an entire large report when only one section changed.
Do not skip backup steps before broad structural edits.

faq.question: What documents is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for long Markdown research reports that need careful structure and citation handling.

faq.question: Does it verify facts by itself?
faq.answer: No. It needs source material from the user to support factual changes.

faq.question: Can it help with legal-style citations?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires new claims to include StableID and page anchors.

faq.question: Does it edit files automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides editing guidance. Actual file changes depend on the AI tool and user permissions.

faq.question: Why does it mention backups?
faq.answer: Backups reduce risk before large edits, restructuring, or report compilation.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex and Claude?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
